questions.title: HQ4: Hadamard-incoherent affine INT4 in a DPAS-operand layout for the dense 27B (EXL3 quality without the trellis)
questions.objective: Give the dense 27B a 4-bit format whose quality matches EXL3 4bpw while decoding in a few instructions per weight, so the decode kernel approaches pin bandwidth instead of 381 GB/s.

scope.excluded: Requant from any quantized artifact, LM-head quantization, W4A4, INT3, changes to the stopped EXL3 kernel program

questions.hypothesis: EXL3's quality comes mainly from block-128 sign+Hadamard incoherence, not from the trellis. Rotated affine INT4 G128 (GPTQ or AutoRound in the rotated basis, INT8 escape for failing tensors, <=4.5 bpw) matches EXL3 block-output KL, and its decode costs a few instructions per weight.

scope.engine: Quality: torch-xpu screen in vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.30.0 on GPU1 (no serving). Speed half: isolated SYCL GEMV microbench on GPU1 only after quality passes
scope.excluded: Serving integration, LM-head quantization, MTP head changes, KV changes, any EXL3 kernel edits (operator-stopped, RL-122)

questions.hypothesis: A 2-stage E8P lattice residual VQ at 4.0 bpw with two-sided block-128 sign-Hadamard incoherence and block LDLQ reaches final-logit KL <= EXL3 4bpw on Qwen3.8-27B, and its table-lookup decode reaches >= 550 GB/s logical GEMV on one B70.
questions.changed_variable: Weight quantizer at ~4 bpw against the EXL3 4bpw trellis reference: E8P 2-stage RVQ (two-sided RHT or residual fold) and scalar sym INT4 G64 (two-sided RHT or residual fold, GPTQ); calibration, eval, canaries, heads, MTP and KV unchanged
questions.smallest_probe: Unsealed 13-layer prefix screen (layers 0-12, 64x512 calibration, 2x832 eval) with arms bf16, exl3, r4_g64, int4_g64_rht, e8rvq4_rht, e8rvq4_fold; then one sealed full 64-layer screen with the same arms. Compile-only ISA price of the E8RVQ4 GEMV before any kernel GPU time.
questions.success_gate: Sanity (else blocked, unscored): fold-exactness probe rel L2 <= 1e-4 on every fold-arm layer; two-sided transform roundtrip rel L2 <= 1e-4 on every RHT-arm layer; EXL3 answers r01 correctly; Hessian inverse deterministic (same input -> torch.equal). R0 gate: best E8 arm has every canary margin correct, eval final-logit KL <= EXL3's and top-1 >= EXL3 - 0.1 pt. K gate: isolated E8RVQ4 GEMV >= 550 GB/s logical at 4.0 bpw for M=1 and M=4 on 5120x17408, 17408x5120 and 5120x12288, outputs within a predeclared relative tolerance of the codec reference. R2: >= 1.30x decode vs EXL3 4bpw in every confirmation pair.
questions.stop_rule: If every E8 arm in the unsealed prefix sits above 1.10x EXL3 KL, skip the sealed run and close E8RVQ4 for this model with the gap recorded. A sealed R0 below the gate closes it. Kernel below 550 GB/s after one layout retry closes the speed half. Failed sanity is blocked, never failed.
questions.uncertainty: QTIP Table 1: E8P at 2 bits has Gaussian MSE 0.089 vs TCQ ~0.069 and D(R) 0.0625, so 2-stage E8 may stay ~1.3x the trellis. Decode cost of E8P lookups on Xe2 is unmeasured. Required kernel gain assumes ~75 % of decode time in the quantized GEMVs. int4_g64_rht needs an online activation Hadamard at serving time.
questions.next_action: CLOSED rejected 2026-10-11 (RL-173). Scalar INT4 with full two-sided incoherence: 2.46x (G64) and 2.84x (G128) EXL3 KL in the 13-layer prefix; E8P 2-stage RVQ killed by Gaussian Monte Carlo at 2.37x D(4). Only a trellis-class quantizer matches EXL3 at 4.0 bpw; successor RQ-29 (XTQ).
questions.economic_gate: Quality first: one GPU1 prefix smoke (~15 min) and one sealed screen (<= 3 h). Kernel GPU time only after the prefix shows E8 KL <= 1.10x EXL3. No download (BF16 + EXL3 on SN770).

questions.title: XTQ: rate-distortion-first trellis 4-bit format with an Xe2-native code decoded into DPAS layout, for the dense 27B
questions.objective: A 4.0 bpw weight format at EXL3 quality (near the Gaussian rate-distortion bound) whose decode runs near the B70 pin bandwidth.

scope.model: Qwen3.8-27B from the BF16 source on SN770; EXL3 4bpw @113cf7ab as quality reference and speed baseline
scope.engine: Quantizer: torch/SYCL on GPU1. Kernel: isolated SYCL GEMV microbench on GPU1. Quality: the RQ-28 screen harness (scripts/tmp/fmt_screen_20261011.py). Serving integration only after K5.
scope.excluded: EXL3 kernel edits (operator-stopped, RL-122), scalar or E8 quantizers (RL-173), LM-head and MTP-head quantization changes, KV changes

questions.hypothesis: A bitshift-trellis quantizer (L=16, K=4, two-sided block-128 sign-Hadamard, block LDLQ) with an Xe2-native code function matches EXL3 4bpw final-logit KL on Qwen3.8-27B, and its decode-into-DPAS-layout GEMV reaches >= 550 GB/s logical at 4.0 bpw on one B70.
questions.changed_variable: Trellis code function and decode kernel layout (EXL3's code and kernel versus an Xe2-native code decoded straight into the DPAS operand layout), quantized by our own Viterbi + LDLQ; incoherence, 4.0 bpw rate, heads, MTP and KV unchanged
questions.smallest_probe: K2: CPU Viterbi MSE of each candidate code at K=4 (L=16, tail-biting) vs the EXL3 code. K3: compile-only Xe2 ISA price of decode-into-DPAS GEMV. K4: GPU1 decode microbench, ring > L2, real shapes. K5: quantize the 13-layer prefix with the chosen code and screen against EXL3 in the RQ-28 harness.
questions.success_gate: K2: best Xe2 code MSE <= 1.05x the EXL3 code's at K=4 [FAILED, RL-176; OPERATOR AMENDMENT 2026-10-12, made after the K2 result and disclosed as such: continue with xe_ih2x2 at its measured 1.099x, because per-tensor allocation is expected to repay ~0.07 bit; the end-to-end K5 quality gate (KL <= EXL3) and K4 speed gate are unchanged]. K3: decode issue per weight >= 1.4x below EXL3's kernel. K4: >= 550 GB/s logical at 4.0 bpw for M=1 and M=4 on 5120x17408, 17408x5120 and 5120x12288 within a predeclared relative tolerance of the torch reference. K5 (quality, sealed full model): every canary margin correct, final-logit KL <= EXL3's and top-1 >= EXL3 - 0.1 pt. R2: >= 1.30x decode vs EXL3 4bpw in every confirmation pair, MTP acceptance within 0.05.
questions.stop_rule: Any K-step below its gate stops the ladder at that step and closes XTQ for this model with the measured number recorded, after at most one retry of an unchanged mechanism. Failed sanity is blocked, never failed.
questions.uncertainty: QTIP reports 1MAD/3INST/HYB within ~3 % MSE, so a cheap code may exist, but Xe2 issue cost per code is unmeasured. Viterbi at L=16 for 26e9 weights may be too slow on one card. The removable share is measured: EXL3 loses 37-43 % of pin inside kernels (RL-119); route gain assumes ~75 % of decode time in quantized GEMVs.
questions.next_action: CLOSED rejected 2026-10-12 at K4 (RL-183): xe_ih2x2 reached 342-420 GB/s (0.69-0.84x of the EXL3 code in the same bench), gate 550; the kernel class is load-bound, so the 1.71x decode-instruction saving (RL-176) does not convert into speed, and the code costs +9.9 % MSE. Kept: the bit-exact trellis quantizer and the ESIMD Viterbi (RL-177, RL-181), usable for EXL3-format artifacts. Re-entry: a B70 GEMV load path that sustains >= 550 GB/s pure-load, or a quality objective (KL-aware rounding) shown to beat EXL3 at equal bits on the 13-layer prefix.
questions.economic_gate: Speed lever is the M=4 verify pass: EXL3 no-spec runs ~470 GB/s (77 % of pin) but MTP3 verify ~380 GB/s (RL-119, RL-174); bringing M=4 to >= 550 GB/s prices EXL3 MTP3 79.9 tok/s post-first to ~1.3-1.44x if ~75 % of round time is quantized GEMV. Stock INT4 is no speed alternative (RL-174). Kernel half priced by ISA before GPU time; quantizer must project <= 8 h on one card; SN770 has ~10 GB free, so the ~16 GB artifact needs space freed first (stock-int4 speed-only checkpoint, 19 GB, is the obvious candidate).

questions.title: EXL3-SC: KL-optimal per-tensor trellis bit allocation for the dense 27B, verified locally and served on the B70
questions.objective: Better final-logit quality than the adopted plain EXL3 4.00bpw at equal or fewer bytes (SC_4.00bpw_H5), or FP8-class quality at ~15 GiB (SC_5.00bpw_H6), served at route speed.

scope.model: Qwen3.8-27B; turboderp/Qwen3.8-27B-exl3 SC_4.00bpw_H5 @4acd9ad5 and SC_5.00bpw_H6 @dfe2f4fd versus plain 4.00bpw @113cf7ab
scope.engine: Quality: layer-streamed harness scripts/tmp/fmt_screen_20261011.py (bit-exact ref.py decode, full 64 layers). Serving: requires mixed-K support in the EXL3 XPU path (operator decision, RL-122 context).
scope.excluded: New quantization runs (exllamav3 convert is CUDA-only), vision-tower quantized V variants

questions.hypothesis: On our harness the SC_4.00bpw_H5 artifact has lower final-logit KL than plain 4.00bpw at equal bytes, and SC_5.00bpw_H6 is within 2x the bf16 noise floor; with mixed-K kernels the SC_4 decode rate equals plain 4.0 within 3 %.
questions.changed_variable: Quantized artifact (uniform K=4 versus per-tensor KL-optimal K in 3..7 with in-domain calibration); engine, MTP, KV, sampling unchanged
questions.smallest_probe: Full-depth harness screen: bf16, exl3 plain 4.0, exl3_sc4, exl3_sc5 on the frozen eval set (final-logit KL, top-1, canary margins). Serving only after an operator decision on mixed-K kernel work.
questions.success_gate: Quality screen: sc4 KL <= 0.85x plain 4.0 KL with top-1 >= plain and all canary margins correct. Route: sealed exact-answer battery pass, decode >= 0.97x plain 4.0 in every confirmation pair (sc4) or quality-tier adoption decision (sc5).
questions.stop_rule: sc4 KL > 0.95x plain on our harness closes the quality claim for this model; a serving build that cannot reach 0.97x plain decode after two attempts closes serving.
questions.uncertainty: Published KLD uses turboderp's in-domain trace; our eval is wikitext-like text plus canaries, where SC recipes may transfer less (optimize.md says wikitext-measured recipes transfer poorly; the reverse direction is untested). Mixed-K serving touches exl3xpu, under the RL-122 operator stop for kernel probes.
questions.next_action: CLOSED 2026-10-13 (RL-203, operator stop on low-impact work): SC5 stays the quality tier at 0.89x plain (RL-179, RL-186); own XTQ quantizer failed three times (RL-191, RL-195, RL-197) and its best case is parity with plain turboderp; SC5 speed fixes bound at ~0.93x (RL-202); MTP5 no gain on real prose (RL-200). Re-entry: a new quantizer mechanism with a written prediction to beat SC5 quality per bit, or a kernel change predicting >=10 % end-to-end. Record: research/2026/stop-decision-low-impact-work-20261013.md.
questions.economic_gate: Quality screen costs ~1 h of GPU1 and 37 GB of T-FORCE disk (73 GB free); no conversion. Serving work is source-level (enable existing K=3/5 templates, add K=7, split mixed fused modules).

portfolio.objective: Reduce time and energy per correctly completed inference task at declared quality and resource limits.
portfolio.selection: Rank meaningful end-to-end benefit, supported mechanism, feasibility, then cost of the deciding probe. No invented success probabilities.
portfolio.minimum_useful_gain: At least 10% for new speed programs unless a stricter route/task gate is declared. Park sub-threshold kernel work.
portfolio.promotion: Fresh paired confirmation plus task-quality evidence and a separate route decision. Diagnostic validation is not an adopted win.
